name: Spain

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 49128297 inhabitants, recorded as 49.128 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Spanish and Catalan, in the transversal venues pass. Four units, four houses, against an opening estimate of 4 produced with no research. The number is the same and the composition is not the one it imagined. Spain, like Italy, has no state list of puppetry venues, and for the same reason: the public money goes to companies and to festivals. What exists instead is a directory kept by the field itself, TiteredData's register of museums, salas, centros and teatros de títeres, and it was the candidate generator. Eighteen entries, of which six are museums and go out under the ruling of 2026-07-28 — Abizanda, the Marionetarium in Barcelona, MITA in Albaida, the Museo del Títere de Cádiz, the Museo Galego da Marioneta, the Museo Taller de Títeres — and one, the Institut del Teatre in Barcelona, is a school. The four that count. The Teatro de Títeres de El Retiro in Madrid, on the Avenida de Méjico, is a municipal space of the Ayuntamiento de Madrid under its Área de Cultura, Turismo y Deporte, and its brief is to be the seat of a puppetry programme of local, national and international reference; it plays every weekend of the year, outdoors and free. TOPIC, at Euskal Herria Plaza in Tolosa, opened in November 2009 out of the Titirijai festival begun in 1983, calls itself the only centre in Europe devoted solely to the art of puppetry, runs a season — 25/26 at the time of reading, with the Titerescena programme of the Centro Dramático Nacional — and shows the Basque Government, the Diputación de Gipuzkoa and the town of Tolosa. Its museum is one of four areas beside theatre, documentation and training, so it is a theatre that keeps a museum and not the reverse. The Centre de Titelles de Lleida, founded in 1986, has occupied the Convent de Santa Teresa since 1996 in premises ceded by the city council, has produced or co-produced some twenty shows and runs the Fira de Titelles with the Ajuntament. The Teatro Arbolé in Zaragoza has built since 1979, opened its first hall in 1990 and moved in 2008 to the Parque del Agua Luis Buñuel; 225 seats, a year-round programme with priority to children's theatre and puppetry, and it appears among the equipment of the Ayuntamiento de Zaragoza. Arbolé is the weakest of the four on vocation, being a children's theatre that came out of puppetry rather than a puppet house. Two salas with their own rooms and resident companies are left out for want of any public backing read: the Sala La Carreta in Elche, 86 seats, owned by the company La Carreta Teatro since 1998, and the Sala Petxina in Valencia, opened in 2008 as the second room of the Teatro de Marionetas la Estrella. Two more from the directory, the Sala Pocas Luces and the Teatre Lluerna, were not read at all. Both omissions run the same way, so four is a floor and the upper bound is set at 8. The Spanish case is worth stating plainly because the map will otherwise mislead. This is a country of companies with rooms, not of institutions with companies, and the indicator sees the second and not the first. Four is what the denominator can prove, not what Spanish puppetry amounts to.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained. Spain has fifteen official higher schools of dramatic art, accredited by the education ministry and awarding qualifications recognised at European level, but their specialisms are Acting, Scenography, and Stage Directing and Dramaturgy: no puppetry specialism. The only foothold identified is the Puppets and Objects module taught at Dantzerti, the Basque higher school of dramatic art in Bilbao. A module within an acting course does not satisfy a denominator that requires a specialised training rather than a subject appearing in a curriculum. The previous value of 0.5 was the midpoint of an estimated range. Caveat: this finding rests on search summaries and an encyclopaedic page, without reading the curricula of all fifteen institutions; confidence therefore stays at estimate and the upper bound at 1. Revisited on 2026-07-27 after the object theatre ruling, which does not change the value but changes what the exclusion has to say. Latvia now counts because object theatre is a named specialisation inside an acting degree; Dantzerti stays out because puppetry there is a subject inside one. That line is now load-bearing for the whole series, so it was checked rather than assumed: the Dantzerti site was opened and lists two degrees, Grado en Arte Dramático and Grado en Danza, with no puppetry or object theatre specialisation named. The exclusion reason is corrected accordingly, from not_degree_granting to outside_denominator, which is the accurate one: Dantzerti does award a state-recognised degree, it simply does not award one in this field. The caveat on the other fourteen ESADs stands unchanged, their curricula having still not been read, and confidence stays at estimated for that reason.

establishments.description: The Basque higher school of dramatic art, one of Spain's fifteen official ESADs. It awards a state-recognised Grado en Arte Dramático, but names no puppetry or object theatre specialisation: the teaching is a module inside the acting curriculum. That is the distinction that separates it from the Latvian case, where object theatre is a specialisation.
